disease_label_per_paper: Acute purulent pericarditis with large pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade
presentation_summary: 65-year-old man with diabetes, hypertension, prior ischemic stroke, and smoking history presented with acute chest pain, worsening dyspnea, productive cough, and high-grade fever for one week.
He was distressed and tachypneic with bilateral dilated neck veins, distant heart sounds, and coarse crepitations.
Vitals showed heart rate 110/min, blood pressure 80/50 mmHg, temperature 39 C, respiratory rate 25/min, and oxygen saturation 92% on room air.
ECG showed sinus tachycardia, low-voltage QRS complexes, and electrical alternans.
Echocardiography showed large circumferential pericardial effusion with early diastolic right ventricular collapse and a dilated noncollapsing IVC, consistent with tamponade.
After emergency pericardiocentesis the WBC was 25 x10^3/uL, CRP was 155 mg/L, and pericardial fluid culture grew Staphylococcus aureus.

quality_warnings: Purulent etiology, S. aureus culture, and antibiotic response are confirmatory or treatment context, not disease-name qualifiers.

The presentation is infectious and shock-like; pericardial effusion, tamponade echo physiology, low voltage/electrical alternans, JVD, and distant heart sounds are retained as the rankable pericardial evidence.
